title.narrative: Increased capacity of constituents to advance gender equality, non-discrimination, inclusion, adequate labour protection and integrated formalization

description.narrative: During the 2024-25 biennium, the ILO is scaling up its interventions through direct policy support, development cooperation projects, and capacity building for institutions. Key initiatives include technical assistance for wage setting mechanisms, advocacy for care economy investments, expansion of health protection programmes, HIV/TB and disability inclusion partnerships with state governments and businesses. By addressing these challenges holistically - recognizing how gender inequality intersects with informal work arrangements, how health status affects employability, and how social protections remain out of reach for most workers - the ILO aims to support India's transition toward a labour market that delivers decent work and social justice for all. The ultimate vision is an inclusive economy where no worker is left behind, whether due to gender, disability, health status or employment type, and where the dignity of all work is properly valued and rewarded.
